01-spreadsheet-basics.md.description: Module 04 — CCC Exam Preparation | Topic 1 --- A spreadsheet is a software application that organizes data in rows and columns, forming a grid of cells. It is used for calculations, data analysis, and creating charts. The most widely used spreadsheet program is Microsoft Excel, which is part of the Microsoft Office suite. 02-cell-addressing-references.md.title: Cell Addressing and References
02-cell-addressing-references.md.description: Module 04 — CCC Exam Preparation | Topic 2 --- When you write a formula in Excel, you refer to cells by their addresses. For example, if you write =A1+B1, Excel uses the values stored in cells A1 and B1 to calculate the result. This is called cell referencing. Cell references are important because they allow formulas to update automatically when data changes. Instead of typing fixed numbers, you refer to cells, and Excel always uses the current...

03-data-entry-editing.md.title: Data Entry and Editing in Excel
03-data-entry-editing.md.description: Module 04 — CCC Exam Preparation | Topic 3 --- In Excel, you can enter three main types of data into cells: Text entries are used for headings, names, descriptions, and other non-numeric data. - Text is left-aligned by default in a cell. - Examples: "Name", "Rahul", "Delhi", "Product A" - If text is longer than the column width, it overflows into the next cell (if that cell is empty) or gets cut off visually. 04-formulas-functions.md.title: Formulas and Functions in Excel
04-formulas-functions.md.description: Module 04 — CCC Exam Preparation | Topic 4 --- A formula is an expression that performs calculations on values in your worksheet. Every formula in Excel must start with an equals sign (=). For example: - =5+3 calculates the sum of 5 and 3 (result: 8) - =A1+B1 adds the values in cells A1 and B1 - =C2*D2 multiplies the values in cells C2 and D2 Excel follows the standard mathematical order of operations: 1. 05-charts-visualization.md.title: Charts and Data Visualization in Excel
05-charts-visualization.md.description: Module 04 — CCC Exam Preparation | Topic 5 --- A chart (also called a graph) is a visual representation of data. Instead of looking at rows of numbers, charts help you see patterns, trends, and comparisons at a glance. In simple words: A chart turns numbers into pictures so that data is easier to understand. Excel provides many types of charts. You select your data and Excel creates the chart for you automatically. CCC Exam Tip: The CCC exam...
